summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, diabetes, and gastroparesis was admitted for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to chronic cholecystitis and right upper quadrant pain. During the same operation, a laparoscopic appendectomy was performed due to uncertain appendiceal findings. The surgeries were uncomplicated. Postoperatively, pain was managed with IV and then oral morphine, with adjustments made for his opioid tolerance. He advanced to a regular diet by postoperative day two, ambulated well, and had no nausea or complications. His diabetes was managed with continued insulin, and his medications were updated, including increased duloxetine and simvastatin doses. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up scheduled in one month and detailed instructions on incision care, activity restrictions, and warning signs to monitor.
problems: Calculus of gallbladder with other cholecystitis, without mention of obstruction
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
